audience.text: Python developers building applications that require programmatic Excel workbook manipulation, especially those needing a permissively licensed, dependency-light alternative to proprietary tools.

capabilities.text: Create new workbooks from scratch or load existing .xlsx files, then modify worksheets, cells, and workbook properties.
capabilities.title: Create and edit workbooks

capabilities.text: Apply fonts, fills, borders, alignment, number formats, and rich text to cells using Style and Font APIs.
capabilities.title: Format cells and ranges

capabilities.text: Handle worksheets, merged cells, hyperlinks, page breaks, tables, shapes, pictures, sparklines, and comments.
capabilities.title: Manage workbook elements

capabilities.text: Create and configure charts and sparklines using Chart, ChartSeries, ChartType, and Sparkline APIs.
capabilities.title: Add charts and sparklines

capabilities.text: Enforce data entry rules using list, number, date, and custom validations, and apply conditional formatting rules.
capabilities.title: Apply data validation and conditional formatting

capabilities.text: Export workbooks to CSV, TSV, JSON, Markdown, and PDF using format-specific save options or inferred file extensions.
capabilities.title: Export to multiple formats

capabilities.text: Protect workbooks with passwords using StandardEncryptionParameters or AgileEncryptionParameters for encryption and decryption.
capabilities.title: Encrypt and decrypt workbooks

capabilities.text: Load CSV data into a workbook using Workbook.load_csv() or load_csv_workbook() with optional CSVLoadOptions.
capabilities.title: Import CSV data

limitations.text: Formula expressions and cached results are preserved, but this project is not a full Excel calculation engine.
Native workbook loading and saving targets the Open XML .xlsx format; other spreadsheet formats such as .xls, .ods, and .xlsb are not supported.
Some advanced Excel features are preserved as source package parts rather than exposed as editable Python objects.
PDF output depends on locally available fonts and the optional skia-python renderer, which is not installed by the core package.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic Excel workbook creation, reading, and modification in pure Python without Microsoft Excel or COM dependencies.
Supports password-protected .xlsx files for secure data handling with encryption and decryption capabilities.
Provides export to multiple formats including CSV, TSV, JSON, Markdown, and PDF for interoperability and reporting.
Supports data validation, conditional formatting, charts, tables, and sparklines to enhance workbook functionality and user experience.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Cells FOSS for Python is a free, open-source, pure-Python library for creating, reading, modifying, and exporting Excel .xlsx workbooks without requiring Microsoft Excel.
